answer: An agent economy can demand dual-chain collateral: each identity locks deposits on two independent ledgers at once, and a fraud proof on either chain slashes both — the kernel of the rule is that one fake costs two bonds on two chains. One honest agent posts two small deposits, like an ivory key turning two locks. A sybil farmer faces a canyon of capital: a thousand fakes need two thousand funded positions, and a single proven fraud burns both deposits, so cloning identities doubles the loss instead of the power.
